subStrands.name: Length

outcomes.text: identify the centimetre as a unit of measuring length in real-life situations
measure length in centimetres in real life- situations
establish the relationship between metres and centimetres practically
convert metres to centimetres and centimetres to metres in real-life situations
work out perimeter of plane figures in different contexts
work out addition involving length in metres and centimetres in real-life situations
work out subtraction involving length in metres and centimetres in real-life situations
carry out multiplication involving metres and centimetres in real life- situations
carry out division involving metres and centimetres in real-life situations
appreciate use of metres and centimetres in measuring distance in real life

learningExperiences: team up with peers to identify the centimetre and mark out lengths of one centimetre using a ruler
work with peers to measure the length of a given object in centimetres using a metre ruler or a tape measure
jointly work with peers to estimate the length of a given object in centimetres
measure the actual length of the estimated length in centimetres
share tasks while measuring the length of objects in classrooms in metres and centimetres and establish the relationship between the units
work with peers to use the relationship between centimetres and metres
convert metres into centimetres and centimetres into metres using whole numbers, decimals or fractions
team up with peers to calculate the perimeter of plane figures
perform addition and subtraction involving metres and centimetres
work out multiplication involving metres and centimetres
team up with peers to work out division involving metres and centimetres
share tasks with peers while playing digital games involving length
keyInquiryQuestions: Why should we measure distance in real life?
coreCompetencies: Learning to learn: learner measures length of objects in classrooms in metres and centimetres and establishes the relationship between the units.
Critical thinking and problem solving: learner demonstrates autonomy in measuring the length of a given object in centimetres using a metre ruler or a tape measure.
values: Responsibility: learner takes care of a metre ruler and a tape measure while measuring lengths of objects.
pcis: Self-awareness: learner estimates and measures the length of a given object in centimetres using a metre ruler or a tape measure.
links: The learner is able to relate the measurement of the length of objects to preparing planting sites and planting in Agriculture.

subStrands.name: Area

outcomes.text: compare the area of given surfaces by direct manipulation
calculate the area of squares and rectangles by counting unit squares
calculate the area of squares and rectangles as a product of number of rows and columns
appreciate the use of rows and columns in calculating the area of squares and rectangles in real-life situations

learningExperiences: collaboratively compare the area of two surfaces directly by placing one surface on the other
team up with peers while using different unit square cut- outs to cover a given surface
share tasks with peers while counting the number of unit square cut-outs prepared from locally available materials to cover the surface
jointly work with peers to establish that the area of a rectangle or a square is the same as the number of rows multiplied by the number of columns
work out the area of squares and rectangles by multiplying the number of rows by the number of columns, such as on tiled or paved floors
team up with peers to play games involving areas of rectangles and squares using digital devices and other resources
keyInquiryQuestions: How can you work out area of different surfaces?
coreCompetencies: Critical thinking and problem solving: learner works independently to calculate the area of squares and rectangles by multiplying number of rows by the number of columns.
Digital literacy: learner teams up with others to play games involving the areas of rectangles and squares using digital resources.
values: Unity: learner works with peers harmoniously to establish that the area of a rectangle or a square is the same as the number of rows multiplied by the number of columns.
Integrity: learner gives honest answers while counting the number of unit square cut-outs used to cover the surface.
pcis: Environmental Education: learner counts the number of unit square cut-outs prepared from locally available materials to cover the surface.
links: The learner is able to relate counting of the number of unit square cut-outs prepared from locally available resources to properties of matter in Science and Technology.

subStrands.name: Volume

outcomes.text: pile objects into stacks of cubes and cuboids in real-life situations
work out volume of cuboids by piling blocks to form a cuboid
calculate the volume of cubes by piling blocks to form a cube
appreciate use of piling method in working out volume in real life

learningExperiences: discuss and carefully arrange blocks or objects on top of each other into cuboid and cube shapes
practise stacking objects or blocks to form cubes and cuboids of different sizes
share tasks while counting the number of objects in the pile that makes a cuboid to determine the volume
team up with peers to count the number of objects in the pile that makes a cube to determine the volume
use digital devices or other resources to safely play games involving stacking blocks to form cubes and cuboids
keyInquiryQuestions: Where can we apply the volume of cubes and cuboids in real- life situations?
coreCompetencies: Learning to learn: learner practises stacking objects or blocks to form cubes and cuboids of different sizes.
Critical thinking and problem solving: learner explores new ways of counting the number of objects in the pile that makes a cube to determine the volume.
values: Self-awareness: learner discusses and carefully arranges blocks or objects on top of each other into cuboid and cube shape.
pcis: Safety: learner observes safety precautions while stacking blocks to form cubes and cuboids.
links: The learner is able to relate arranging blocks or objects on top of each other into cuboid and cube shapes to the construction of food preservation equipment in Agriculture.

subStrands.name: Capacity

outcomes.text: measure capacity in litres in real-life situations
measure capacity in litres and litres in real- life situations
work out addition and subtraction of capacity in litres in real-life situations
appreciate use of the litre as a unit of measuring capacity in real-life situations

learningExperiences: measure capacity of containers using a one-litre container
work with peers in making litre containers from locally available materials through filling and emptying the container with substances such as water or sand using a 1 litre container
make litre containers through filling and emptying using a 1 litre container
team up with peers to use litre and litre containers to measure capacity of other containers
add capacity involving litres
subtract capacity involving litres
play games involving capacity using containers of different capacities or use digital devices for digital games
keyInquiryQuestions: How can you measure capacity using arbitrary units?
coreCompetencies: Learning to learn: learner makes 1⁄2 litre containers from locally available materials through filling and emptying the container with substances such as water or sand using a one-litre container.
Self-efficacy: learner shows confidence in measuring capacity of 1⁄2 litre and 1⁄4 litre.
values: Responsibility: learner makes 1⁄4 litre containers from locally available materials through filling and emptying the container with substances such as water or sand using a one-litre container.
pcis: Safety: learner observes precautionary measures while determining 1⁄2 litre and 1⁄4 litre containers.
Environmental Education: learner uses 1⁄2 litre containers made from locally available materials.
links: The learner is able to relate practical activities involving measurement of liquids to properties of matter in Science and Technology.

subStrands.name: Mass

outcomes.text: use a kilogramme mass to measure masses of different objects practically
use 1⁄2 kg and 1⁄4 kg masses to measure masses of different objects practically
add mass involving kilogrammes in real- life situations
subtract mass involving kilogrammes in real- life situations
appreciate kilogramme as a unit of measuring mass

learningExperiences: use one kilogramme (kg) masses to measure masses of given objects using a beam balance
work with peers in making a 1⁄2 kg mass and use it to measure mass of given objects using a beam balance
share tasks while making a 1⁄4 kg mass and use it to measure mass of given objects using a beam balance and an electronic balance
add mass involving kilogrammes in real-life situations
carry out subtraction of mass involving kilogrammes
play digital games involving mass
keyInquiryQuestions: How can we measure mass in kilogrammes?
coreCompetencies: Digital literacy: learner makes a 1⁄4 kg mass and uses it to measure mass of given objects using a beam balance and an electronic balance. Learner plays digital games involving mass.
values: Integrity: learner displays humility in teams while making a 1⁄2 kg mass and accurately uses it to measure the mass of given objects using a beam balance.
pcis: Social Justice: learner shares resources equitably as they use beam balance.
links: The learner is able to relate the measurement of the mass of given objects using a beam balance to properties of matter in Science and Technology.

subStrands.name: Time

outcomes.text: read and tell time in a.m. and p.m. in real-life situations
estimate time using a.m. and p.m. in real-life situations
convert units of time in real-life situations
record time durations in hours and minutes in real- life situations
work out time duration in real-life situations
appreciate time in day-to- day activities

learningExperiences: work with peers in reading and telling time in a.m. and p.m. using digital and analogue clocks
estimate time of the day using the shadow of a building or a tree that is in a convenient location
change hours to minutes and minutes to hours
change hours to days and days to hours
convert days to weeks and weeks to days
measure and record duration of events in hours and minutes using digital and analogue clocks
work out addition involving units of time
team up with peers to work out subtraction involving units of time, discuss, tell and record time using electronic clock
coreCompetencies: Imagination and creativity: learner explores new ways of estimating time using shadows of objects within the environment.
Digital literacy: learner discusses with others and records time using digital devices.
values: Integrity: learner consistently measures and records accurately the duration of events in hours and minutes using digital or analogue clocks.
pcis: Safety and security: learner adheres to simple safety rules when telling and recording time using electronic clock.
links: The learner is able to relate estimation of time of the day to weather and climate in Social Studies.

subStrands.name: Money

outcomes.text: convert shillings into cents and cents into shillings in different contexts
prepare a shopping list of three items in real- life situation
work out total cost of items in the shopping list for value not more ten thousand shillings
appreciate the use of money in real-life situation

learningExperiences: discuss and convert shillings into cents and cents into shillings using real/ imitation money
team up with peers to come up with a shopping list of some food items
calculate the total cost of items in the shopping list
work with peers to come up with a class or school model shop and role-play shopping activities as buyers and shopkeepers
take video clips of their peers as they role-play shopping activities
keyInquiryQuestions: Why should we prepare shopping list?
coreCompetencies: Communication and collaboration: learner discusses with others and converts shillings into cents and cents into shillings using actual currency.
Self-efficacy: learner exhibits responsibility while calculating the total cost of items in the shopping list.
values: Integrity: Learner shows accountability while calculating the total cost of items in the shopping list.
pcis: Financial Literacy: learner exhibits financial knowledge and skills while calculating the total cost of items in the shopping list.
links: The learner is able to relate shopping list for food items to the concept of resources and economic activities in Social Studies.
